title: Time provision verifier exposes mutable rollback and board-identity trust anchors
description: Security review: ProvisionVerifier.expected_board_identity and minimum_record_version are public writable attributes, and public persist_version(version) can be called directly with a lower version. Any caller holding the verifier can retarget the board identity or lower/persist the rollback floor without authenticated metadata evaluation. Make trust anchors immutable/private; expose only monotonic internal advancement after successful validation; reject non-increasing/direct downgrade attempts and add tampering regressions.
notes:
Independent correctness probe: minimum_record_version=2; calling persist_version(0) succeeds, then verifier-issued version-0 metadata is accepted. Acceptance must cover lower/equal/higher versions and persistence callback failure.
Concurrency finding: evaluate_epoch_floor reads the mutable floor, persists, then assigns without a lock. Concurrent version-2/version-3 records can persist/commit 3 and then regress in-memory minimum to 2. Lock verify-persist-commit-clear as one transaction and concurrency-test out-of-order callbacks.
Same-version rollback also exists: after accepting version 2 at epoch F+100, a different version-2 record at F+50 is accepted because only version<minimum is checked. Persist (version, canonical record digest/epoch); equal version is valid only for the identical record, and changed content requires a strictly newer version.
